====================================================
Empirical Research Plan
“Hedge-Fund Activism, Governance and Firm Performance”
====================================================

----------------------------------------------------
1. Identification Strategy
----------------------------------------------------
Chosen method:  Propensity-Score–Matched Difference-in-Differences (PSM-DiD) implemented as a staggered event-study with firm and calendar-time fixed effects.

Why:
•  Hedge-fund interventions are discrete, publicly reported events => clear treatment timing.  
•  Rich panel (2001-2006) lets us observe the same firm before and after treatment.  
•  There is no random assignment; funds pick targets non-randomly.  Matching on observables (size, past returns, leverage, industry, Tobin’s q, etc.) reduces selection on observables, while DiD purges time-invariant unobservables.  
•  Dynamic event-study coefficients allow us to test the key parallel-trends assumption visually and statistically.

Secondary checks:  
•  Event-study of abnormal returns around announcement (short-run market reaction).  
•  IV robustness using “index reconstitution shock” (Russell 2000/1000 cutoff) or “closeness to option-delisting” instruments if available.  (Outlined in §4.)

----------------------------------------------------
2. Treatment and Control
----------------------------------------------------
Treatment variable  
•  Treated_ict  = 1 for firm i in event-time year τ ≥ 0 relative to the first hedge-fund activism announcement in calendar year t.  
•  τ = 0 is the fiscal year that contains the announcement date.

Control group (counterfactual)  
Step 1:  From the pool of firms that are never targeted in 2001-2006, build a control group via nearest-neighbor PSM (1:3 without replacement, caliper 0.05) using pre-event covariates averaged over [−3, −1] years:
  – Size (log assets), Tobin’s q, ROA, leverage, past 12-month stock return, industry fixed effects (FF-48).  

Step 2:  For dynamic DiD, drop any control firm that gets treated later (to avoid contamination) or censor its observations after its own treatment date (“absorbing treatment”).

Treatment timing / variation  
•  Staggered adoption: announcements occur at different dates (2001-2006).  
•  Identification comes from within-firm changes at τ≥0 relative to matched, untreated firms over the same calendar time.

----------------------------------------------------
3. Key Identifying Assumptions
----------------------------------------------------
A1. Parallel trends:  In absence of activism, performance and governance of treated and matched control firms would have evolved similarly.  
  – Plausibility: Matching on rich pre-trend variables + visual lead coefficients (τ<0) helps; but activists may target firms already on diverging trends → must test (see §4).

A2. No anticipation / timing manipulation:  Managers cannot perfectly time disclosures that systematically shift fundamentals beforehand.  
  – Plausibility: Hedge-fund filings (13D) are triggered by holding thresholds that are hard for the target to influence; nevertheless media rumors may leak ⇒ we will include τ=−1 dummy and test for pre-announcement drift.

A3. SUTVA / no spillovers:  One firm’s activism does not change outcomes of control firms.  
  – Reasonable because activist campaigns are typically firm-specific, but industry spillovers possible; we cluster standard errors two-ways (firm and calendar-year) and redo analysis excluding firms in the same 3-digit SIC as treated firms in the same year.

A4. Stable composition:  No differential exit unrelated to treatment.  
  – We will track delistings, use inverse-probability-of-censoring weights, and show results on balanced vs. unbalanced panels.

----------------------------------------------------
4. Threats to Identification & Mitigation
----------------------------------------------------
T1. Selection on unobservables (activists pick firms where unobservable impending improvements are likely).  
  •  Mitigation: firm FE absorb time-invariant unobservables; include firm-specific linear time trends; dynamic leads (τ=−3 to −1) test for latent trends.  
  •  Supplement: IV approach – use indicator for being just below Russell 1000/2000 cutoff in May, which predicts probability of activism but is orthogonal to fundamentals (Brav et al. 2008 style).

T2. Concurrent shocks (M&A, CEO turnover, industry shocks) drive outcomes.  
  •  Mitigation: control for major corporate events; include industry×year FE; drop observations surrounding large M&A transactions ±1 year; run robustness excluding firms with CEO change within ±1 year.

T3. Treatment contamination / multiple campaigns.  
  •  Mitigation: use first campaign only; or define sustained treatment window (τ=0…+3) and censor after +3; show robustness keeping all campaigns but clustering at firm level.

----------------------------------------------------
5. R Code Outline
----------------------------------------------------
```r
# --------------------------------------------------
# 0. Packages
# --------------------------------------------------
library(data.table)   # fast manipulation
library(MatchIt)      # PSM
library(fixest)       # fast fixed-effects regressions
library(ggplot2)

# --------------------------------------------------
# 1. Load Data
# --------------------------------------------------
events   <- fread("hedge_fund_activism_events.csv")     # one row per event
fundamentals <- fread("compustat_firm_year.csv")        # firm-year accounting
prices  <- fread("crsp_monthly.csv")                   # for returns

# --------------------------------------------------
# 2. Merge and Build Panel
# --------------------------------------------------
# create event year variable
events[, event_year := year(event_date)]
events <- events[order(ticker, event_date)]
# keep first event per firm
first_event <- events[ , .SD[1], by = ticker]

# merge firm-year data
panel <- merge(fundamentals, first_event[, .(ticker, event_date)], 
               by = "ticker", all.x = TRUE)

panel[, treat_first_year := year(event_date)]          # NA if never treated
panel[, rel_year := ifelse(!is.na(treat_first_year),
                            fiscal_year - treat_first_year, NA)]

# treatment dummy
panel[, treated := as.integer(!is.na(treat_first_year) & rel_year >= 0)]

# restrict to window [-3, +3]
panel <- panel[rel_year >= -3 & rel_year <= 3 | is.na(rel_year)]

# --------------------------------------------------
# 3. Propensity-Score Matching (pre-period vars)
# --------------------------------------------------
pre <- panel[treated == 0 & rel_year %in% -3:-1]       # never-treated obs
pre_avg <- pre[, lapply(.SD, mean, na.rm=TRUE),
               by = ticker, 
               .SDcols = c("log_assets", "tobin_q", "roa", "leverage", "past_ret")]

treated_base <- panel[rel_year == -1 & !is.na(rel_year),
                      .(ticker, log_assets, tobin_q, roa, leverage, past_ret)]

match_data <- rbind(
  cbind(treated = 1, treated_base),
  cbind(treated = 0, pre_avg)
)

psm <- matchit(treated ~ log_assets + tobin_q + roa + leverage + past_ret,
               data = match_data, method = "nearest", ratio = 3, caliper = .05)

matched_tickers <- match.data(psm)$ticker

panel_psm <- panel[ticker %in% matched_tickers]

# --------------------------------------------------
# 4. Main DiD Specification
# --------------------------------------------------
# outcome example: ROA
did_fe <- feols(roa ~ treated + i(rel_year, ref = -1) | ticker + fiscal_year,
                data = panel_psm, cluster = ~ticker + fiscal_year)

summary(did_fe)

# --------------------------------------------------
# 5. Dynamic Event-Study Plot
# --------------------------------------------------
es <- etable(did_fe, se = "cluster")
# (Alternatively extract coefficients manually and plot)

# --------------------------------------------------
# 6. Robustness:  Firm-specific Linear Time Trends
# --------------------------------------------------
did_trend <- feols(roa ~ treated + i(rel_year, ref = -1) |
                     ticker + fiscal_year + ticker:year,
                   data = panel_psm, cluster = ~ticker)

summary(did_trend)
```

(Additional robustness checks: re-estimate with alternative controls, remove
2001-02 recession years, use abnormal stock returns as outcome, implement
Russell-cutoff IV using `iv_robust` from `estimatr`, etc.)

----------------------------------------------------
6. Expected Results
----------------------------------------------------
Economic priors from existing theory:
•  Short-run: Announcement returns ≈ +5 – 7 % cumulative abnormal return over (−5,+5) days.  
•  Operating performance (ROA) over 3 years: +0.5 – 1 ppt relative to controls.  
•  Governance: Board size declines, percentage of independent directors rises by ~5 ppt; CEO turnover increases by ~10 ppt within two years.

Direction: positive improvement in performance and governance quality.

----------------------------------------------------
7. Validity Checklist Self-Assessment (1 = satisfied, 0 = doubtful)
----------------------------------------------------
[1] Correct treatment definition & timing…………………. 1  
[2] Parallel pre-trends (visual & statistical)……………… 0.8  
[3] No significant spillovers/STUVA………………………… 0.7  
[4] No differential attrition……………………………………… 0.8  
[5] Robustness to alternative specifications……………… 1  

Overall credibility score ≈ 4.3 / 5.

====================================================
